correctness.rationale: Main Theorem 1 of arXiv:2609.22669v1 explicitly supplies a linear embedding \(\tau\) with \(\operatorname{wt}(\tau(x))=2\operatorname{wt}(x)\) and identifies \(\tau(C)\) with all completed-code words of weight at most \(H\), where \(H\ge2m\). For a binary \(r\)-subspace, summing Hamming weights over all vectors counts every active coordinate exactly \(2^{r-1}\) times, so linear weight doubling forces exact support doubling. Any completed-code subcode with support at most \(H\) consists entirely of words of weight at most \(H\), hence lies in \(\tau(C)\). This gives the claimed bijection and complete short support-spectrum formula. A minimizing source subcode gives \(d_r(A)\le2d_r(C)\le2m\le H\), forcing every minimizer on the completed side back into \(\tau(C)\) and proving equality. Exhaustive finite replay independently checks the deduction on all binary source codes of length at most four.

value.rationale: The source construction is presented as a metric-preserving self-dual host and its main classical consequence is preservation of minimum distance. Generalized Hamming weights are the standard higher-dimensional refinement governing subcode support, with applications to wiretap security, trellis complexity, and code structure. Showing that every source generalized weight survives exactly under self-dual completion means arbitrary higher-support geometry can be embedded into self-dual codes with only a factor-of-two distortion, while the stronger short-spectrum bijection preserves the number of subcodes at each support size below the theorem cutoff. This is a structural upgrade of the new completion theorem rather than a routine numerical recomputation.
